claim: Huang and Vaughan establish two mean-value theorems for the number of solutions of a/n=1/x+1/y, one with a fixed and n varying, one with both a and n varying.
stance_target: state of the art for two-term (binary) unit-fraction equation counting, named explicitly in the research task as a canonical reference
quoted_support: In this paper, we establish two mean value theorems for the number of solutions of the Diophantine equation a/n=1/x+1/y, in the case when a is fixed and n varies and in the case when both a and n vary.

claim: The Huang-Vaughan results are one order lower (two-term, not three-term) than Section 5's problem and, like the other asymptotic-counting literature, count multiplicities of a single representation rather than coincidences between two independently varying triples matched on two symmetric functions.
stance_target: direct applicability of Huang-Vaughan's technique to Section 5's problem
quoted_support: we establish two mean value theorems for the number of solutions of the Diophantine equation a/n=1/x+1/y
